paraphrase: Karma is threefold: accumulated (sañcita), to come (āgāmi) and begun (prārabdha). Knowledge burns the accumulated; the to-come does not cling to the knower, as water does not cling to a lotus leaf; the begun is exhausted by experience. The knower's future merit goes to those who serve and praise him, his demerit to those who revile him.
notes: Attributed to Śaṅkara (attribution traditional or disputed).

paraphrase: The six virtues defined: śama is control of the mind; dama control of the outer senses; uparati is the observance of one's own dharma; titikṣā is endurance of heat and cold, pleasure and pain; śraddhā is trust in the words of guru and Vedānta; samādhāna is one-pointedness of mind.
notes: Note the definition of uparati as performance of one's own dharma, where the Vivekacūḍāmaṇi defines it as the mind not leaning on externals. Attributed to Śaṅkara (doubtful).

paraphrase: The gross body is made of the quintuplicated elements and is the seat of experience; the subtle body of seventeen members (five organs of knowledge, five of action, five prāṇas, mind and intellect) made of the unquintuplicated elements, is the instrument of experience; the causal body is indescribable, beginningless ignorance.
notes: Attributed to Śaṅkara (attribution traditional or disputed).
